title: Sentences that describe nouns
titleJp: ぼうしを かぶっている 人は だれ？
canDo: I can describe a person by what they are doing or wearing (あかい ぼうしを かぶっている 人) and ask who they are.
I can talk about things and places through what happened with them: 母が 作った ケーキ, せんしゅう 行った レストラン.
I can build a described noun from English: find the core noun, put it at the end and put the whole description before it.
I can take apart a long Japanese sentence: find the ★ predicate, the core noun and the description attached to it.
I can use が (not は) for the subject inside the description.

blocks.t: Warm-up: 5 sentences with 〜ている from lesson 07-1, out loud (ぼうしを かぶっています, 本を 読んでいます…)
Vocabulary: tap 🔊 on each word and repeat it twice
Grammar 4a: the description comes before the noun, reading the examples aloud
Grammar 4b: が inside the description, with one 🔬 on each example
Grammar 4c: building and taking apart in your notebook, step by step
Video (block 6): the part on clauses that describe nouns
Notebook homework + checking it against the answer key (if you split the lesson: 4a–4b + h1 in one session; 4c + h2–h4 in the other)
Checklist (block 10) + write your questions in the lesson notebook

skills: Present and past short forms (lessons 08-1 and 09-1): only short forms go before the noun.
〜ている for actions in progress and for states (lesson 07-1), including clothes and accessories: めがねを かけている, ぼうしを かぶっている.
Adjective + noun (lesson 05-1): 高い 本. This lesson works the same way — only now the "adjective" is a whole sentence.
N₁ の N₂ (lesson 01-1): the describing part comes first and the core comes last.

vocab.en: to put on (glasses): めがねを かける
to put on (something on your head): ぼうしを かぶる
to put on, to wear (clothes above the waist)
to put on, to wear (shoes, or clothes below the waist)
to live (somewhere): 〜に すんでいる (I live in…)
to cross (a street, a bridge): はしを わたる
police box (a small neighborhood police station)

grammar.title: Clause + noun
grammar.gloss: the whole description comes BEFORE the noun
grammar.explanation:
In English, the description comes **after** the noun and usually starts with "that / who / which": "the present **that I got**", "the person **who is wearing a hat**". Japanese does the opposite: the whole description comes **before** the noun, and **there is no word for "that / who / which"**. The last verb of the description touches the noun directly.
• もらった + プレゼント → もらった プレゼント (the present I got)
• ぼうしを かぶっている + 人 → ぼうしを かぶっている 人 (the person wearing a hat)
• Only **short forms** go inside the description: 見る, 見た, 見ない, 見なかった, 見ている.
• Here a verb works **just like an adjective**: it sits in the same slot an adjective or N の uses: 高い レストラン, サンパウロの レストラン, せんしゅう 行った レストラン. Everything that describes sits on the left; the **core** (the thing you are talking about) comes last.
• The whole block works as **one single noun**: it can take は, を, に or come before です.
• The core is often a very general noun — 人 (person), もの (thing), ところ (place): きのう 見た もの (the things I saw yesterday), はしを わたった ところ (the spot right after you cross the bridge).
• For clothes and accessories someone has on, use 〜ている: めがねを かけている 人 is "the person wearing glasses".
grammar.structure: [description in short form] [core noun] — the core comes at the END of the block

examples.jp: あかい ぼうしを かぶっている 人は だれですか。
examples.kana: あかい ぼうしを かぶっている ひとは だれですか。
examples.romaji: Akai bōshi o kabutte iru hito wa dare desu ka.
examples.en: Who is the person wearing a red hat?

examples.jp: これは たんじょうびに もらった プレゼントです。
examples.kana: これは たんじょうびに もらった プレゼントです。
examples.romaji: Kore wa tanjōbi ni moratta purezento desu.
examples.en: This is a present I got on my birthday.

examples.jp: せんしゅう 行った レストランは 高かったです。
examples.kana: せんしゅう いった レストランは たかかったです。
examples.romaji: Senshū itta resutoran wa takakatta desu.
examples.en: The restaurant I went to last week was expensive.

pitfalls: No の between the verb and the noun: もらったの プレゼント ✗ → もらった プレゼント ✓. の only goes between two nouns.
Don't put the description after the noun, the way English does: 人 ぼうしを かぶっている ✗ → ぼうしを かぶっている 人 ✓.
No です／ます inside the description: もらいました プレゼント ✗ → もらった プレゼント ✓. です／ます only goes at the very end of the whole sentence.
For clothes someone has on, use 〜ている. For "the person wearing glasses": めがねを かける 人 ✗ → めがねを かけている 人 ✓. めがねを かける 人 would be "a person who puts on glasses" (as a habit, or later).
howToStudy: Cover the noun at the end of each description and ask "which one?". The answer is everything to its left.

Tap 🔬: the verb right before the noun shows up as DESCRIBES NEXT, the same label as あかい and N の. The blocks before that verb (ぼうしを as OBJECT, たんじょうびに as TIME) belong to the description: in your notebook, put brackets from the start of the description up to that verb.
Speaking: describe 5 people around you or in a photo out loud: [clothing]を [verb]ている 人が います。

grammar.title: Inside the description, the subject takes が
grammar.gloss: が stays inside; は stays outside
grammar.explanation:
When the description has its own subject (who did it, who lives there), that subject takes **が**, not は. は says "this is what I'm talking about", and it frames the **whole sentence**. A description is only a label stuck onto one noun — it isn't talking about anything by itself — so inside it the subject goes with が, the plain subject marker.
• Whole sentence: 母**は** ケーキを 作りました。 (My mother made a cake.)
• Turned into a description of ケーキ: 母**が** 作った ケーキ (the cake my mother made). は became が, ケーキ moved to the end and its を disappeared.
• The big sentence can have its own は, outside the description: 母が 作った ケーキ**は** おいしかったです。 That は marks the whole block: "as for the cake my mother made…".
• When the subject is obvious (you yourself), it can disappear: もらった プレゼント.
• You will sometimes hear の instead of this が (父の すんでいた 家). That is normal — inside a description, の is allowed to mark the subject — but for now use が.
grammar.structure: [subject] が [short verb] [core] は／を／です — が stays inside, は stays outside

examples.jp: これは 父が すんでいた 家です。
examples.kana: これは ちちが すんでいた いえです。
examples.romaji: Kore wa chichi ga sunde ita ie desu.
examples.en: This is the house where my father used to live.

examples.jp: 母が 作った ケーキは おいしかったです。
examples.kana: ははが つくった ケーキは おいしかったです。
examples.romaji: Haha ga tsukutta kēki wa oishikatta desu.
examples.en: The cake my mother made was delicious.

examples.jp: マリアさんが 書いた さくぶんを 読みました。
examples.kana: マリアさんが かいた さくぶんを よみました。
examples.romaji: Maria-san ga kaita sakubun o yomimashita.
examples.en: I read the essay Maria wrote.

pitfalls: The number-one mistake is using は inside the description: 母は 作った ケーキ ✗ → 母が 作った ケーキ ✓.
One sentence, two roles: in 母が 作った ケーキは おいしかったです, the one who made it is your mother (が, inside), but the topic is the cake (は, outside). Ask yourself: who MADE it? What WAS delicious?
This が is not the "but" が from lesson 08-3. That one comes after a complete sentence (〜ですが、…); this one comes right after a noun (母が).
howToStudy: Turn 3 は sentences into descriptions. E.g. 父は この 家に すんでいました → 父が すんでいた 家. Change は to が, move the core to the end and delete its particle.
Tap 🔬 on example 2: 母が shows up as SUBJECT and 作った as DESCRIBES NEXT. That SUBJECT belongs to the description; the TOPIC of the big sentence is ケーキは.
Speaking: say 3 sentences about things in your home, following the model [person]が 作った / 書いた [thing]です。

grammar.title: Building and taking apart
grammar.gloss: a step-by-step method for the Japanese order
grammar.explanation:
The grammar is simple; the hard part is the **order**. Always use the same steps.
**Building (English → Japanese)**, e.g. "the book the teacher wrote":
• 1) Find the **core**, the thing you are talking about: "book" (本).
• 2) Write the description as a complete short sentence: 先生が 本を 書いた.
• 3) Take the core out of it. **Its particle leaves with it**: 先生が 書いた.
• 4) Attach the core at the end: 先生が 書いた 本.
• 5) Use the block as a single noun: 先生が 書いた 本を 読みました。
**Taking apart (Japanese → English):**
• 1) Read the ★ predicate at the end of the sentence.
• 2) Look for a short-form verb **right before a noun**: a description ends there, and that noun is the core.
• 3) Go back to the left: the blocks with が, を, に, で just before that verb usually belong to the description. A block with は almost always stays outside, because it belongs to the big sentence.
• 4) Translate starting from the core: core + "who / that / where / with whom" + description. English puts the core first, so you read the Japanese block backwards: [こうばんの 前で 本を 読んでいる] 人 = the person [who is reading a book in front of the police box].
• In 🔬, the verb that closes a description shows up as **DESCRIBES NEXT**: that is your sign that a description ends there.
• Going further (Sakubi): when descriptions pile up, a sentence can sometimes be bracketed in two ways. 白い ぼうしを かぶっている 男の子の お父さん can be "the father of [the boy in the white hat]" or "[the boy's father], who is wearing the white hat". Native speakers pick the reading with common sense and context, and so will you: if your brackets give a strange meaning, try another split.
grammar.structure: build: core → short sentence → take out the core and its particle → attach the core at the end · take apart: ★ → short verb + noun → go back to the start of the description

examples.jp: こうばんの 前で 本を 読んでいる 人は 私の 父です。
examples.kana: こうばんの まえで ほんを よんでいる ひとは わたしの ちちです。
examples.romaji: Kōban no mae de hon o yonde iru hito wa watashi no chichi desu.
examples.en: The person reading a book in front of the police box is my father.

examples.jp: あの 白い シャツを きている 男の人は、きのう 話した 先生です。
examples.kana: あの しろい シャツを きている おとこのひとは、きのう はなした せんせいです。
examples.romaji: Ano shiroi shatsu o kite iru otoko no hito wa, kinō hanashita sensei desu.
examples.en: That man in the white shirt is the teacher I talked to yesterday.

examples.jp: はしを わたった ところに 小さい きっさてんが あります。
examples.kana: はしを わたった ところに ちいさい きっさてんが あります。
examples.romaji: Hashi o watatta tokoro ni chiisai kissaten ga arimasu.
examples.en: Right after you cross the bridge, there's a small café. [lit. at the place where (you) have crossed the bridge, there is a small café]

pitfalls: Don't stop at the first noun: in こうばんの 前で 本を 読んでいる 人は…, the core is not こうばん or 本. It is 人, the noun right after the verb.
Don't repeat the core inside the description: 先生が 本を 書いた 本 ✗ → 先生が 書いた 本 ✓.

English "that", "where" and "with whom" turn into nothing: きのう 話した 先生 = the teacher I talked with yesterday; 父が すんでいた 家 = the house where my father lived. Don't add と or に to stand in for them: と 話した 先生 ✗ → 話した 先生 ✓.

If your short sentence (step 2) ends in だ, that だ can't touch the core: まちは しずかだ → しずかだ まち ✗ → しずかな まち ✓ (with a noun, の: がくせいの 人). In the past, だった is fine: むかし しずかだった まち ✓ (the town that used to be quiet).
howToStudy: In your notebook, copy the 3 examples, underline the ★ predicate, circle the core and put brackets around the description: [こうばんの 前で 本を 読んでいる] 人.

Sentence mining: in Wagotabi or a graded reader, find one sentence with a description before a noun. Look up the words you don't know (Jisho.org, or the Yomitan pop-up for text in your browser), bracket the description, and save the sentence in ヅオリンゴー → Mining.
ヅオリンゴー → Drills → 🔬 Anatomy → 🔬 Analyze: paste example 2 and find the two verbs marked DESCRIBES NEXT (きている → 男の人; 話した → 先生). あの, 白い and 男の are marked DESCRIBES NEXT too, but they are not verbs.

homework.intro: Do it by hand in your notebook. The training here is about order: before writing each item, find the core noun and write it last. Only then open the answer key, item by item. Circle what you got wrong and redo it the next day.

tasks.prompt: Build the block in Japanese: only the described noun, without です. Follow the steps in point 4c.

items.q: the person wearing a black hat

a.jp: くろい ぼうしを かぶっている 人
a.kana: くろい ぼうしを かぶっている ひと
a.romaji: kuroi bōshi o kabutte iru hito

a.jp: めがねを かけている 女の人
a.kana: めがねを かけている おんなのひと
a.romaji: megane o kakete iru onna no hito

a.jp: 私が 作った ケーキ
a.kana: わたしが つくった ケーキ

items.note: When it is you, 私が can drop: 作った ケーキ.

a.jp: アナさんが すんでいる まち

items.note: まちに すんでいる: when まち becomes the core, the に disappears.

items.q: the present I got from my father

a.jp: 父に もらった プレゼント
a.kana: ちちに もらった プレゼント

items.note: With もらう, the giver takes に. The receiver (me) is understood.

a.jp: 白い くつを はいている 男の子
a.kana: しろい くつを はいている おとこのこ
a.romaji: shiroi kutsu o haite iru otoko no ko

tasks.prompt: Put the blocks in order to make the sentence. Tip: start with the ★ predicate and the core noun, and build the description to the left of the core.

items.q: 【人は】【ギターを】【だれですか】【ひいている】

a.jp: ギターを ひいている 人は だれですか。
a.kana: ギターを ひいている ひとは だれですか。
a.romaji: Gitā o hiite iru hito wa dare desu ka.
a.en: Who is the person playing the guitar?

items.q: 【ケーキです】【作った】【これは】【ルーカスさんが】

a.jp: これは ルーカスさんが 作った ケーキです。
a.kana: これは ルーカスさんが つくった ケーキです。
a.romaji: Kore wa Rūkasu-san ga tsukutta kēki desu.
a.en: This is the cake Lucas made.

items.q: 【しゃしんを】【見ました】【アナさんが】【とった】

a.jp: アナさんが とった しゃしんを 見ました。
a.kana: アナさんが とった しゃしんを みました。
a.romaji: Ana-san ga totta shashin o mimashita.
a.en: I looked at the photos Ana took.

items.q: 【こうさてんを】【ところに】【わたった】【あります】【こうばんが】

a.jp: こうさてんを わたった ところに こうばんが あります。
a.romaji: Kōsaten o watatta tokoro ni kōban ga arimasu.
a.en: Right after you cross the intersection, there's a police box.

items.q: 【かぶきは】【おもしろかったです】【せんげつ】【見た】

a.jp: せんげつ 見た かぶきは おもしろかったです。
a.kana: せんげつ みた かぶきは おもしろかったです。
a.romaji: Sengetsu mita kabuki wa omoshirokatta desu.
a.en: The kabuki I saw last month was interesting.

items.note: せんげつ stays inside the description: last month is when I SAW it.

items.q: 【まちです】【しずかだった】【ここは】【むかし】

a.jp: ここは むかし しずかだった まちです。
a.romaji: Koko wa mukashi shizuka datta machi desu.
a.en: This is a town that used to be quiet.

items.note: むかし belongs to the description (when was it quiet?). Past だった can touch the noun; in the present it would be しずかな まち, never しずかだ まち.

tasks.prompt: Take each sentence apart: write the core noun with its description in brackets, and translate the whole sentence into English.

items.q: あそこで 電話を している 女の人は だれですか。

a.jp: ［あそこで 電話を している］ 女の人
a.kana: ［あそこで でんわを している］ おんなのひと
a.romaji: [asoko de denwa o shite iru] onna no hito
a.en: Who is the woman talking on the phone over there?

items.note: Core: 女の人, right after the verb している.

items.q: 友だちが 作った ブラジルりょうりを 食べました。

a.jp: ［友だちが 作った］ ブラジルりょうり
a.kana: ［ともだちが つくった］ ブラジルりょうり
a.en: I ate the Brazilian food my friend made.

items.note: 友だちが is the SUBJECT of the description (who made it). The one who ate is me.

items.q: 私が 行った ちゅうがっこうは とても 古かったです。

a.jp: ［私が 行った］ ちゅうがっこう
a.kana: ［わたしが いった］ ちゅうがっこう
a.en: The junior high school I went to was very old.

items.q: きのう こうさてんで 会った 人は すずきさんの お母さんでした。

a.jp: ［きのう こうさてんで 会った］ 人
a.kana: ［きのう こうさてんで あった］ ひと
a.en: The person I met at the intersection yesterday was Suzuki's mother.

items.note: The time block (きのう) and the place block (こうさてんで) before the verb belong to the description.

tasks.prompt: Write 4 sentences about the place where you live and the people there. Use a description before a noun in at least 3 sentences, with が inside at least one of them. Then read them aloud.

items.q: Model (match its structure, not its words):

a.jp: 私の 家が ある まちには 古い はしが あります。はしの 前に 小さい こうばんが あります。こうばんの 前で いつも 新聞を 読んでいる おじいさんは 私の 友だちです。きのう 母が 作った ケーキを いっしょに 食べました。
a.kana: わたしの いえが ある まちには ふるい はしが あります。はしの まえに ちいさい こうばんが あります。こうばんの まえで いつも しんぶんを よんでいる おじいさんは わたしの ともだちです。きのう ははが つくった ケーキを いっしょに たべました。
a.romaji: Watashi no ie ga aru machi ni wa furui hashi ga arimasu. Hashi no mae ni chiisai kōban ga arimasu. Kōban no mae de itsumo shinbun o yonde iru ojiisan wa watashi no tomodachi desu. Kinō haha ga tsukutta kēki o issho ni tabemashita.
a.en: In the town where my house is, there is an old bridge. In front of the bridge there is a small police box. The old man who is always reading the newspaper in front of the police box is my friend. Yesterday we ate together the cake my mother made.

items.note: Check: the core at the end of each block, no です／ます inside a description, and the description's subject with が.

workbook.tip: Do it after points 4a–4c. Take each sentence apart in your notebook before answering. Check it with the official Genki Answer Key.

practice.what: Play normally and hunt the dialogues for a short-form verb right before a noun (〜た 人, 〜ている もの…). Copy 2 into your notebook, bracket the description and translate. Then log the session in Immersion → Games and paste one of those lines into Anatomy.

Your reviews first (🌊 All gathers every review due today, Lesson 9 words included). Then Drills → 🔬 Anatomy → 🧱 Build from the end: 5 sentences. At each DESCRIBES NEXT block, say out loud which noun is the core.
Journal: write your homework h4 sentences and open "Anatomy of what I wrote". The verb before each described noun should show up as DESCRIBES NEXT; if it doesn't, check the order.

Resources tab → Tadoku's free graded readers: read one level-0 or level-1 story and hunt for 3 descriptions before a noun (a short-form verb right before a noun). Bracket them in your notebook. Don't look up every word: follow the story.
Look at a photo with several people and describe 5 of them out loud: [clothing]を [verb]ている 人が います。 Record it and listen.

culture.title: Gifts and wrapping
culture.body: In Japan, the **wrapping** is part of the gift. In department stores and many smaller shops, the clerk often asks whether it is a present and wraps it on the spot, with paper and ribbon, usually at no extra cost. Formal gifts, such as the summer and year-end gifts (お中元 and お歳暮), are often wrapped with **のし** paper, which has decorative cords called **水引** (みずひき, mizuhiki). Another tradition is the **ふろしき**, a square cloth that wraps and carries a gift and can be used again. When you hand a gift over, use **both hands**; the person receiving it often asks あけても いいですか。 before opening it. In general, people avoid giving sets of 4 or 9 items, because し sounds like the word for "death" and く like the word for "suffering".
culture.try: Wrap an object in a square cloth, ふろしき style (search "furoshiki otsukai tsutsumi" to see the basic knot). Then practice handing it over out loud, with both hands: これ、私が 作った ケーキです。どうぞ。

checklist: I put the whole description BEFORE the noun, with no word for "that / who" and no の.
I use only short forms inside the description (見る, 見た, 見ている, 見なかった), never です／ます — and never a present だ right before the noun (しずかな まち, but しずかだった まち).
I use が (not は) for the subject inside the description.
I can describe people by their clothes with 〜ている (ぼうしを かぶっている 人) without looking.
I can take apart a long sentence: find the ★ predicate, circle the core and bracket the description.
I can build a block from English following the steps: core → short sentence → take out the core → attach it at the end.
I did the homework, checked it against the answer key and redid what I got wrong.
